cases.description: Members sort at every depth, arrays keep their order, and no white space is written.
Names sort as strings, not as numbers, and a name sorts before every longer name that begins with it.
Characters outside ASCII are written as UTF-8, never escaped, whether or not the input escapes them.
A quotation mark and a backslash are always escaped with a backslash.
Backspace, tab, line feed, form feed and carriage return are written as \b, \t, \n, \f and \r.
Every other character from U+0000 to U+001F is written as \u and four lowercase hexadecimal digits.
A solidus is never escaped, and characters from U+007F on are written as they are, the controls among them included.
Zero is written 0, and so is minus zero.
The largest integers a double holds exactly, 2^53 - 1 and its negative, are written in full.
An integer written with a fraction or an exponent is written as a plain integer.
1E23 is the double 0x44b52d02c7e14af6 of RFC 8785, Appendix B, written 1e+23.
0.0000010 is the double 0x3eb0c6f7a0b5ed8d of RFC 8785, Appendix B, written 0.000001.
10^21 in full is the double 0x444b1ae4d6e2ef50 of RFC 8785, Appendix B, written 1e+21: it is the first power of ten written with an exponent.
2^68 in full is the double 0x4430000000000000 of RFC 8785, Appendix B, written as its shortest digits followed by zeros.
5E-324 is the smallest positive double, 0x0000000000000001 in RFC 8785, Appendix B, written 5e-324.
-1.7976931348623157E308 is the most negative finite double, 0xffefffffffffffff in RFC 8785, Appendix B, written -1.7976931348623157e+308.
The literals true, false and null are written as they are, and an empty object or array has nothing between its brackets.
A lone surrogate in a string has no canonical form.
A lone surrogate in a member name has no canonical form.
